faq.title: Questions Enterprise Buyers Ask
faq.subtitle: The questions your security, legal, and infrastructure teams will ask in the first meeting — answered here so you arrive prepared.

questions.q: Where does our data actually live?
questions.a: Wherever you put it. Veritas deploys into your VPC, on-premises datacenter, or air-gapped environment. Data residency is jurisdiction-pinned per namespace and enforced at the infrastructure layer. Your data never transits a Veritas-controlled cloud unless you explicitly choose a private-cloud deployment — and even then, it is isolated to a single-tenant instance under your control.

Every generated output is grounded exclusively in your proprietary corpus and carries a verifiable source citation. Ungrounded claims are rejected at the guardrail layer before delivery — not flagged after the fact. We do not claim zero error across all possible queries; we claim that no output reaches your users without a traceable, defensible source. That is the standard legal, financial, and healthcare teams require — and it is what we contract to.

questions.q: Do you train your models on our data?
questions.a: No — contractually and architecturally. Your proprietary data is never used to train, fine-tune, or improve any shared or foundation model. Per-tenant model isolation means your workloads never share inference paths or weight state with another customer. This is enforced at the infrastructure layer, not buried in a privacy policy clause.

questions.q: How long does a full deployment take?
questions.a: A typical production rollout runs 12–24 weeks end-to-end: ~2 weeks for discovery and architecture review, 4–8 weeks for a scoped pilot against a representative workload, then 8–16 weeks for full production rollout with phased tenant onboarding. Air-gapped and highly regulated environments trend toward the upper end. We do not rush compliance.

questions.q: What does the audit trail actually prove?
questions.a: Every inference, agent action, and data access is written to a tamper-evident, cryptographically chained log. For any query we can reconstruct: who asked it, what context was retrieved, what was generated, what guardrail validated it, and when each step occurred. The trail is exportable to your SIEM in real time and admissible as evidence to regulators and courts.

questions.q: What happens if your company disappears?
questions.a: Because Veritas runs inside your perimeter on your infrastructure, a vendor outage does not take your platform down. Source-availability and operational runbook escrow are standard contract terms — your team can operate the platform independently. Sovereign deployment means the platform's survival is not coupled to the vendor's.

story.title: Sovereign AI for the Regulated Enterprise
paragraphs: Veritas Global AI was founded on a simple observation: most enterprise AI vendors host your data on shared infrastructure and call it secure. That wasn't good enough for the institutions we'd worked with — global financial firms, national healthcare systems, and sovereign governments where accuracy is non-negotiable.

Our team has deployed mission-critical AI inside the most regulated environments on earth. We've seen what works, what doesn't, and where the waste happens. We built Veritas to do it differently: deploy to the client, never the other way around.

The name — Veritas, Latin for truth — reflects our founding belief. Every model we deploy is grounded exclusively in your data. Every output carries a verifiable citation. Every inference is cryptographically logged. Trustworthy AI starts with trustworthy infrastructure.

sections.title: 1. Our Commitment to Security
paragraphs: At Veritas Global AI, security is foundational to everything we build. As a provider of enterprise AI infrastructure deployed inside our clients' perimeters, we understand that trust is earned through rigorous security practices, transparent disclosure, and continuous improvement.
This Security Disclosure outlines our security posture, the measures we take to protect data, and how security researchers and the public can responsibly report vulnerabilities.

sections.title: 2. Security Architecture
paragraphs: Our enterprise platform is built on the following security principles:
items: Sovereign Deployment: All client AI workloads run inside the client's own VPC, on-premises infrastructure, or air-gapped environment. No data transits a vendor cloud the client has not authorized.
Zero Shared Tenancy: Each client deployment operates in complete isolation. There is no shared tenancy, no shared inference path, and no vendor-side model access to client data.
Data-at-Rest Encryption: All stored data is encrypted using AES-256 encryption.
Data-in-Transit Encryption: All network communications use TLS 1.3 with strong cipher suites.
Role-Based Access Control: Granular, auditable access controls at every layer of the stack.
Immutable Audit Logs: All actions are logged to tamper-evident audit trails with cryptographic verification.
Never Trains on Client Data: Client data is never used to train, fine-tune, or improve our models.

sections.title: 3. Compliance Framework
paragraphs: Our platform is designed to meet or exceed the following standards:
items: SOC 2 Type II
GDPR
HIPAA (where applicable)
FedRAMP-Ready architecture

sections.title: 4. Responsible Disclosure Policy
paragraphs: We believe that working with skilled security researchers helps us identify and address vulnerabilities before they can be exploited. If you discover a security vulnerability in our systems, websites, or products, we encourage you to report it to us responsibly.

sections.title: 5. Guidelines for Researchers
paragraphs: When conducting security research, we ask that you:
items: Make a good faith effort to avoid privacy violations, destruction of data, and interruption or degradation of our services.
Do not access, modify, or delete data that does not belong to you.
Give us a reasonable amount of time to address the issue before public disclosure.
Do not exploit a vulnerability beyond what is necessary to demonstrate its existence.
Do not engage in social engineering, phishing, or physical security testing of our offices or data centers.

sections.title: 6. Scope
paragraphs: This disclosure policy applies to:
items: veritasglobalai.tech and all associated subdomains
Veritas Global AI web applications and APIs
Veritas Global AI enterprise platform software
extraParagraphs: The following are out of scope:
extraItems: Third-party services and applications not operated by Veritas Global AI
Vulnerabilities in client-managed infrastructure or configurations
Social engineering attacks targeting our employees or contractors

sections.title: 7. How to Report a Vulnerability
paragraphs: Please send vulnerability reports to:
Your report should include:
items: A detailed description of the vulnerability
Steps to reproduce the issue

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: This Cookie Policy explains how Veritas Global AI ("we," "us," or "our") uses cookies and similar tracking technologies on our website veritasglobalai.tech (the "Site"). It explains what these technologies are, why we use them, and your rights to control our use of them.

This policy complies with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the ePrivacy Directive (Cookie Law), the UK GDPR, the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and other applicable privacy and data protection laws.

sections.title: 2. What Are Cookies?
paragraphs: Cookies are small text files that are placed on your device (computer, smartphone, tablet) when you visit a website. They are widely used to make websites work efficiently, to remember your preferences, and to provide information to the website owners.
Cookies may be either:
items: First-party cookies: Set directly by the website you are visiting. Only that website can read them.
Third-party cookies: Set by a domain other than the website you are visiting, typically used for advertising, analytics, or embedded content.
Session cookies: Temporary cookies that expire when you close your browser.
Persistent cookies: Remain on your device for a set period or until you manually delete them.
extraParagraphs: In addition to cookies, we may also use similar technologies such as local storage, session storage, and server logs. In this policy, we refer to all these technologies collectively as "cookies."

sections.title: 4. Third-Party Cookies
paragraphs: Our Site may include content or functionality from trusted third-party service providers. These third parties may set their own cookies when you interact with their embedded content. We do not control the placement of these cookies, and we recommend reviewing the cookie policies of any third-party services. Currently, our Site uses:
items: Netlify: Our hosting provider may set essential cookies for load balancing, security, and site delivery optimization.
Google Fonts: We use Google Fonts for typography. Google may collect information about your use of this service.
extraParagraphs: We regularly review our third-party integrations and will update this list as our service providers change. We select providers that comply with applicable data protection laws and provide adequate safeguards.

sections.title: 5. Cookie Consent and Control
paragraphs: When you first visit our Site, you are presented with a cookie consent banner that allows you to accept or manage your cookie preferences. You can change your preferences at any time.
In addition to our consent management tool, you can control cookies through:
items: Browser Settings: Most web browsers allow you to control cookies through their settings. You can set your browser to refuse all or some cookies, or to alert you when cookies are being sent. Note that disabling strictly necessary cookies may affect Site functionality.
Browser Extensions: Privacy-focused browser extensions can help you manage and block tracking cookies.

Do Not Track (DNT): Some browsers include a Do Not Track feature. Our Site currently does not respond to DNT signals, but we respect cookie consent preferences set through our consent management tool.
Opt-Out Tools: Industry bodies such as the Network Advertising Initiative (NAI) and the Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) provide opt-out tools for targeted advertising cookies.

Legitimate Interests (Art. 6(1)(f)): For strictly necessary cookies essential to Site operation and security. We have conducted a legitimate interest assessment and determined that these cookies are necessary and proportionate.
